items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he said, "I'm Frank Sinatra" and he says "You hungry?"

ctx.x: Meade Lux Albert Ammons they had Meade Lux Lewis, Alan Edwards, Joe Turner, Pete Johnson, and the Harry James band, and Frank Sinatra was singing with them. And I don't know -- I hope I don't get in no trouble for saying it, but I met him, and we come back stage and the guys were saying just stand here, they were playing; they had just broadcasted -- they were broadcasting nightly -- and Sinatra was just talking to them; he said, "I'm Frank Sinatra" and he says "You hungry?" and I said, "Yeah" and he went back…

And after he came back from singing he says, "I'm gonna be a big star one of these days. This is my last week, and I'm going with Tommy Dorsey." And I was amazed that he'd even talk to me, you know. Like I said, I was just a kid, and being on the South Side, you didn't fraternize too much with the white people, you know.

I'll never forget it, though, he gave me a picture -- I lost that picture back in 1955; somebody stole my belongings, because I had messed up; if they didn't steal them then I left them there, never did find them misplaced them. But I moved out of this room, -- but I remember that; we went out that night, and oh my God, we played, we sang "The Lamp is Low" -- I'll never forget the routine we did. "The Lamp is Low" -- we did "The Sheik of Arabee" and we closed with "Tiger Rag" which we used as a flash, and we…
